how_customers_find_and_choose: Business buyers find makers through trade contacts, referrals, exhibitions and increasingly through online business directories and chat
Buyers ask for samples, photos or short videos of the product and the factory floor before a visit
Reliability on quality, delivery time and honest communication decides repeat orders more than the lowest quote
Export buyers check certifications, past orders and responsiveness; local buyers lean on reputation and credit terms
what_works_now: A short product catalogue or sample set with clear specifications, easy to send in chat
Photo and video proof of the factory floor, process and finished lots shared with buyers
Giving buyers an order status update before they ask: in production, packed, dispatched
Written order sheets with quantity, specification, date and agreed terms so disputes are rare
Tracking rejections and rework by cause so the same fault is not repeated
Planning raw material orders against confirmed orders, not hope
A complete company listing online with address, product range and contact
outdated_or_weak: Relying only on a few big buyers with no second source of orders
Hand-written orders and verbal promises that nobody can check later
Generic marketing advice made for consumer shops, such as social media daily posts or discount offers
Waiting for buyers to arrive at trade fairs as the only lead source
Quoting from memory with no record of material cost changes

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Power and gas supply interruptions and raw material price swings affect planning
Export units follow buyer compliance and shipping deadlines closely; credit terms between businesses are long and cash flow is a constant concern
Eid holidays close many units for days; labour availability dips around them
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Many factories are in industrial zones and free zones with their own licensing rules; the owner asks the zone authority
Local manufacturing is often for re-export, regional supply or construction demand
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Smaller makers often serve specialty or custom niches and sell online and through local shops
Product safety, labelling and environmental rules apply by sector; the owner checks with the relevant authority

never_assume: A website or a product catalogue
A sales team or a dedicated person handling enquiries
